key_concepts: input 2 and later source CHOP blending
proportional, difference, quaternion, and additive methods
base input behavior in Difference mode
output interval follows the weight input
zero-weight source inputs do not cook
common_gotchas: Input 1 is the weight/control CHOP; blended source CHOPs begin at input 2.
There should be one blend channel for each source input, except when Difference mode omits the base weight.
The output interval follows the first input, not the blended source inputs.
Quaternion blending expects channels to be grouped as quaternion attributes, commonly via Attribute CHOP.
Zero-weight source inputs may not cook, so avoid relying on their side effects.
